title: Glob guards correctly distinguish zero/under-threshold matches from healthy coverage, including literal and recursive patterns
statement: devai policy check glob guards MUST report a guard as failing when its pattern's match count is below its declared min_matches (default 1), including when the pattern's base directory does not exist at all. It MUST report a guard as passing when the match count meets or exceeds min_matches. Literal (glob-metacharacter-free) patterns MUST be evaluated as a direct file-existence check, not as a directory walk. The evaluator MUST NOT descend into node_modules or .git when resolving matches.
rationale: The tool exists specifically to catch config drift where a glob silently degrades to matching nothing (or less than expected) while whatever consumes it keeps reporting green — found via stynx's devai-gates.yml (docs/architecture/invariants/*.json went to zero matches after a rename, guarded by a defensive `[ -f ... ] || continue` that made the whole validation step a silent no-op) and pec's generate-test-obligations.mjs (an .md-only, non-recursive scan silently dropped invariants already migrated to devai's canonical .json format). A glob-guard checker that itself gets these classification boundaries wrong (zero vs. under-threshold vs. healthy, literal vs. glob, or that walks into node_modules and reports false-positive matches) would fail to catch the exact bug class it was built for.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
